FIX BUG #374: resume, conclude, operator and ten more commands ignore the realm map's journal that run and inspect use

You are fixing exactly one bug from the code-health epic (#330) on branch fix-374-journal-resolution, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text is below and is the whole framing: its "Fix" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Where the issue says the operator rules between options, implement the option the issue recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say in your result notes which option you took so the pull request can ask for the ruling.

RULES
- Scope: fix this bug and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites.
- Tests: add or extend the suite that proves the fix. Assert exact values and exact error variants or text, never is_err() alone. Show every new test binds: make a compiling mutation that removes the fix, run the test and see it fail, restore the fix, and record the failing test name in your notes.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new line and branch reachable by a test. If a branch cannot be reached deterministically, restructure rather than leave it uncovered.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Gates before you report complete, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test for every crate you touched (crate-scoped: cargo test -p <crate>); git diff --check.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#374)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

THE ISSUE (#374), verbatim:

Found by the code-health sweep (epic #330). Verified on `main` at `8da75ed1`/`ba52724e` (2026-09-25).

## What happens

Which journal a command opens depends on the command. `cli_args.rs` has 12× `realms: Option<PathBuf>`, 11× `db: Option<PathBuf>`, and 11× `db: PathBuf` defaulting to `DEFAULT_DB`.

| Behaviour | Commands |
|---|---|
| Honour the realm map's journal | run, tui, inspect, seats, watch, transcript, export, import, runs, realms, muninn run, operator supersede |
| **Ignore it and use `DEFAULT_DB`** | resume, rerun, conclude, operator retry/stop, costs, replay, ledger, anchor, keep-refs, compare, bridge, ui, doctor's database check |

- `rerun` pins the map's world (`World::discover`) but writes to `DEFAULT_DB`.
- `DEFAULT_DB`'s own doc (`crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs:51-63`) calls the map-named shared journal the normal setup.

## Why it matters

In a mapped world, which is the normal setup:
- After `brokkr run` lands a run in the map's journal, `brokkr resume`, `brokkr conclude` and `brokkr operator retry/stop` look in the wrong file by default. **The recovery verbs fail exactly when they are needed.** Operators currently work around this by always passing `--db`.
- `brokkr ui` shows a different fleet from `brokkr tui`.

## Fix

- Introduce a `JournalArgs { realms, db }` parameter object, flattened into every command's args and resolved once. Add `RunSelector::{Readout, Exact}` to encode decision 0015.
- This changes behaviour for 13 commands in mapped worlds, so **it needs an operator ruling**. Land the refactor with a per-command legacy mode, then flip it.

## Acceptance

- In a fixture world with a realm map, run → resume → conclude → operator stop all address the same journal with no `--db`.
- `ui` and `tui` list the same fleet.

This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: Fixed #374 in one signed commit 6b7d1d4b on fix-374-journal-resolution. It is not pushed. OPTION TAKEN (the PR must ask for the ruling): the issue suggests landing the refactor in legacy mode and flipping it later. The acceptance criteria need the flipped behaviour, so this commit lands the flip directly. The old default is still available by typing `--db .forge/forge.db`; no legacy flag was added. WHAT CHANGED: a new `JournalArgs { realms, db }` in cli_args.rs is flattened into 13 verbs: resume, rerun, conclude, operator, costs, replay, ledger, anchor, keep-refs plant/list/delete, compare, bridge and ui. Each resolves its journal once through `JournalArgs::journal`, using Invocation's rules: `--db` beats the map's journal, and with neither the default is .forge/forge.db. These journal-only verbs read the map with Invocation::inspect, so a moved crossing does not block conclude or operator stop. resume still refuses a moved crossing through its pinned-world fence (the existing test a_moved_crossing_refuses_run_rerun_and_resume_before_any_seat_spawns still passes). rerun uses Invocation::resolve because it pins the world; before this change it discovered the map's world but wrote to the default journal. doctor's `--db` is now optional, and its database line checks the map's journal. operator retry/stop now accept `--realms`, and the refusal text is now exactly "--findings, --by-run, --by-seq and --by-realm belong to 'supersede'; 'retry' takes --run, --reason, --realms and --db" (asserted with assert_eq). TESTS: (1) tests/realms.rs the_recovery_verbs_address_the_maps_journal_with_no_db. In a fixture world with a realm map and no `--db` anywhere: run parks (exit 2); resume (exit 2); operator stop (exit 0, last event OperatorAccepted in state/world.db); conclude (exit 3, last event RunStopped); costs, replay, ledger and compare (exit 0); rerun (exit 2, a second run in the map's journal); doctor prints '<world.db> opens'; .forge/forge.db is never created. (2) src/tests.rs ui_and_tui_open_the_journal_the_map_names asserts the journal ui serves equals tui's single hearth, <ws>/state/world.db. MUTATION PROOFS, each run and then restored: making JournalArgs::journal return db-or-DEFAULT_DB failed test 1 at the resume step ('run ... not found', left Some(1) right Some(2)) and failed test 2 (left ".forge/forge.db", right "/tmp/.../state/world.db"). Pointing the conclude arm at DEFAULT_DB failed test 1 at conclude (Some(1) vs Some(3)). Pointing operator at DEFAULT_DB failed test 1 at realms.rs:483 (Some(1) vs Some(0)). Pointing rerun's store at DEFAULT_DB failed at the rerun step ('loading source run ... not found'). Making doctor's map arm unreachable failed at the doctor assertion (realms.rs:512). GATES run in this session: cargo fmt --all -- --check OK; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings OK; cargo test -p brokkr-cli gave 32 of 32 suites ok (lib 469 passed; realms 16 passed); git diff --check OK; compile --bundle bundles/self OK. Only brokkr-cli was touched, so no other crate was tested and no witness digest moved (the witness_journal suite passed). PENDING: scripts/coverage-exact.sh (the controller runs it). New branches: the doctor match arms (Ok(Some) is covered by the mapped doctor run; the default arm by the mapless doctor tests in init_doctor.rs); JournalArgs::journal is covered by every flipped verb. FOLLOW-UPS, deliberately not in this diff: (a) RunSelector::{Readout, Exact} for decision 0015, which the issue's Fix names, was not added because the bug does not need it. (b) The twelve verbs that already honoured the map (tui, inspect, seats, watch, transcript, export, import, runs, realms, supersede) still carry their own realms/db fields and journal_of; moving them onto JournalArgs is a pure refactor. (c) inspect, seats, watch and export resolve with Invocation::resolve, so a moved crossing refuses them, while the new journal-only verbs do not refuse; the operator may want these unified. (d) In a many-hearth world, ui still serves one journal (the map's top-level one) while tui tabs every hearth, so 'same fleet' holds only for single-hearth worlds.

cargo test --workspace: 75 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Lower-priority notes (not severity-bearing): the issue's Fix asked for a per-command legacy mode and RunSelector::{Readout,Exact}; neither landed, and no decision document was added even though the commit changes the default journal of 13 verbs (the PR must ask for the operator ruling). Also pre-existing, out of scope for #374: brokkr run with no --db writes to the world journal even when the operated realm names its own (0026 ruling 1), and the fleet notice on stderr names world.db while runs/tui list realm journals. members.correctness: Correctness/fit review of 6b7d1d4b (cli: every journal verb opens the map's journal (#374)), the only commit over origin/main. Tests bind: under pre-fix resolution operator stop would open .forge/forge.db, fail, and leave default.exists() true (verified by reading the resolution path against the assertions; no mutation run by this seat). Gates run here: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings clean; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --locked and --all-features --locked = 788 passed 0 failed; git diff --check clean. Diff touches only crates/brokkr-cli; frozen surfaces, hosts and witness digests untouched. No security finding from this seat. Findings: [low] The issue's second Fix clause is unimplemented: no RunSelector::{Readout, Exact} type exists anywhere (grep over crates/ and docs/ is empty); selector behavior remains the pre-existing ad-hoc split (read verbs resolve_run, write verbs literal) with no behavioral consequence. [low] The issue's landing plan was not followed: it prescribes landing with a per-command legacy mode and then flipping; this commit flips all 13 verbs at once, with --db .forge/forge.db as the only old-behavior escape (commit message asks for the operator ruling at PR). [low] Three guide passages now state the pre-fix behavior this commit removes: docs/guides/read-surfaces.md:50-54 (resume/conclude/rerun/doctor/ui/costs/compare/anchor/bridge 'still take --db alone ... resumed by naming that journal with --db'), docs/guides/quickstart.md:533-535 (resume 'takes no --realms'), quickstart.md:600-601 (costs 'takes no --realms', --db 'defaults to .forge/forge.db'), quickstart.md:648-654 ('--realms reaches only some commands'), and quickstart.md:167-168 (doctor db default now map-dependent). [info] No proposed decision document accompanies this semantic default change (house rule; precedent 0062/0063). [info] ui/tui fleet equality holds where the world has one hearth; in a v2 multi-hearth world ui still serves a single journal while tui lists every hearth (pre-existing serve_ui shape, not worsened). [info] JournalArgs is flattened into the 13 flipped verbs only; the 11 already-correct verbs and DoctorArgs keep inline realms/db with duplicated doc text - a deliberate targeted-edit scope line. Option taken for the PR ruling: direct flip without a per-command legacy mode, old default reproducible with --db .forge/forge.db.

result.notes: Chief synthesis for 6b7d1d4b (cli: every journal verb opens the map's journal (#374)). Panel result residual/medium, no security residual, no spec defect; this verdict holds that floor and does not lower it. PANEL SHAPE: the brief names the positions correctness and security, but the panel's members are correctness and adversarial. Both returned valid verdicts (residual), and both state they found no security issue. Neither position's text addresses the gate or argues for a result, so no injection finding. MY OWN READ: I read the full diff (cli_args.rs, lib.rs, doctor.rs, the tests), Invocation::resolve/inspect/open (lib.rs:1596-1725), World::discover/inspect/journal/hearths (brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs:407-561) and the resume fence (lib.rs:2284-2286). The core fix is sound. The 13 verbs resolve the journal as --db, else the map's journal, else .forge/forge.db. Resume still runs verify_crossings on its pinned world. Rerun now resolves strictly, before any store opens. Conclude and operator stop/retry read the map leniently for the journal path only, and pin no world. In this session I ran: cargo test -p brokkr-cli --locked --test realms the_recovery_verbs_address_the_maps_journal_with_no_db (1 passed), and cargo test -p brokkr-cli --locked --lib ui_and_tui_open_the_journal_the_map_names (1 passed). Security read: no new write path or fence bypass, so no security residual. SURVIVING FINDINGS, one list for the reforge: (1) [medium] raised by adversarial; correctness raised it as info. Acceptance bullet 2, 'ui and tui list the same fleet', holds only in a one-hearth world. ui serves world.journal() (lib.rs:2131, then JournalArgs::journal at lib.rs:1821-1825), while tui and runs open world.hearths(), one journal per realm (hearths_of, then realms.rs:544-561). In a v2 map where realms name their own journals, the two surfaces are disjoint. The new unit test uses only a one-realm v1 map, so it cannot see this. I confirmed the code paths by reading them; I did not rerun the adversarial's hand-built v2 workspace. My addition to the same finding: ui reads the map leniently (Invocation::inspect) while tui reads it strictly (fleet_of with Invocation::resolve), so in a moved-crossing world tui refuses while ui serves. (2) [low] raised by correctness and adversarial. The issue's Fix is only partly implemented. No RunSelector::{Readout, Exact} was added. No per-command legacy mode was added either: all 13 verbs flip at once, and --db .forge/forge.db is the only way back to the old default. Option taken, which the PR must put to the operator for a ruling: the direct flip. (3) [low] raised by correctness; I confirmed it with sed. The guides still describe the pre-fix behaviour: docs/guides/read-surfaces.md:50-54, and docs/guides/quickstart.md:167-168 (doctor --db default), 533-535 (resume takes no --realms), 600-601 (costs takes no --realms) and 648-654 ('--realms reaches only some commands'). My addition: the World::inspect doc (brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs:410-412) says only doctor, realms and muninn run read the world that way, 'and nothing else'. JournalArgs::journal now reads it that way for 13 verbs, including the writing verbs conclude and operator stop/retry. (4) [info] raised by correctness and adversarial. This changes the default journal of 13 verbs, but no proposed decision document accompanies it, which the house rule asks for. (5) [info] raised by adversarial; pre-existing and out of scope. In a v2 map, run with no --db writes to the world journal even when the operated realm names its own journal. PENDING, not observed by this seat: the full workspace test suite, clippy and fmt (the panel reports them clean; I did not rerun them), the exact-coverage gate, and the implementer's mutation evidence that the tests bind (the correctness member reasoned about it and did not run a mutation).

Reforge of 6b7d1d4b answering review findings 1-4. The single amended commit is c42feca5 (signed, %G? = G), 'cli: every journal verb opens the map's journal (#374)'. It is not pushed. (1) [medium] ui vs tui in many-hearth worlds: ui now resolves through the new ui_journal (lib.rs), which calls hearths_of, the strict Invocation::resolve path that tui uses. It serves the single hearth, or refuses with exact text naming every hearth journal and pointing to --db. This also closes the lenient/strict mismatch the chief added. New test: tests::ui_refuses_a_world_of_two_hearths_that_tui_reads_whole. It builds a v2 map with alpha.db and beta.db, asserts tui opens [alpha, beta], and asserts ui's exact error string. Binding: I mutated Cmd::Ui back to journal.journal(workspace), and 'cargo test -p brokkr-cli --locked --lib ui_' printed 'ui_refuses_a_world_of_two_hearths_that_tui_reads_whole ... FAILED' (panic at tests.rs:786, the serve closure) with 9 passed and 1 failed. I restored the fix and the test passed. (2) [low] Option taken: the DIRECT FLIP. I added no per-command legacy mode and no RunSelector::{Readout, Exact}. Decision 0070 (proposed) records the choice and asks the operator to rule on it. Why: acceptance needs the flipped default, and a mode nobody selects would be dead code under the exact-coverage gate. RunSelector encodes decision 0015's prefix scope, which this change does not alter, so it is left as a follow-up. (3) [low] docs: I updated docs/guides/read-surfaces.md, docs/guides/quickstart.md (doctor --db default, the resume flags, costs --realms, and the 'reaches only some commands' limit, now replaced by a 'ui serves one journal' limit), and the World::inspect doc in brokkr-runtime/src/realms.rs.
